title: Vintage Gibson J-200 Value Guide: Prices Through 1979
description: Vintage Gibson J-200 values through 1979, with annual postwar price references, repair and originality context, and six photographs from my own archive.
alt: Sunburst SJ-200 with floral pickguard and open moustache bridge in a pink-lined case

faqs.q: How Much Is A 1950s Gibson J-200 Worth?
faqs.a: The 2025 published reference for a 1950 to 1959 standard J-200 is $16,500 to $21,500 in all-original excellent condition with its original case. I reviewed that reference alongside historical completed comparisons as of October 2026. It isn't a guaranteed offer or a claim that every recent sale reaches that range.

faqs.q: What Is A 1970s J-200 Artist Worth?
faqs.a: The shared published reference for 1970 to 1979 J-200 examples is $4,750 to $6,250 in all-original excellent condition with the original case. Completed comparisons include altered and repaired guitars below that reference. Confirm the exact model and its construction before applying the table.

faqs.q: Why Is There No Prewar Price Band?
faqs.a: I haven't verified enough independent ordinary-market completed sales to support a prewar range under this guide's evidence standard. A published book range, an advertised price and a celebrity-associated result don't establish that band together. Prewar examples need individual research.

No. In SJ-200, SJ identifies the Super Jumbo family. Gibson's Southern Jumbo is a different model. I wouldn't apply this table to a Southern Jumbo merely because a label or description uses the initials SJ.

faqs.q: Does A Converted Saddle Increase Value?
faqs.a: A conversion may suit a player's preferences, but it changes the comparison with an original collector example. I need to know what was changed, what remains inside the guitar and whether the removed parts survive. There isn't a fixed premium for a conversion.

faqs.q: Does A Quality Refret Remove All-Original Status?
faqs.a: Under this site's grading approach, a quality refret preserves the all-original classification of an otherwise original guitar and removes museum-quality status. Neck reshaping, refinishing and structural repairs are separate conditions.

No. The table identifies a dated published reference checked against completed-sale records. Current advertised inventory isn't used as a realized transaction. A purchase offer and an owner's net proceeds are also different from the reference range.
